title: Fourier transform of an irreducible middle extension
statement:
In the conventions of [rem-dl-a1-conventions], let $\psi$ be a
nontrivial additive character of $k_0$, let
$j:U_0\hookrightarrow A_0$ be a dense open immersion and let
$\mathcal M$ be a nonzero irreducible lisse Weil sheaf on $U_0$ which is
constituent-nonexceptional in the sense of
[def-a1-constituent-nonexceptional]. Then there are a dense open
immersion $j':U'_0\hookrightarrow A'_0$ into the dual line and a nonzero
irreducible lisse Weil sheaf $\mathcal M'$ on $U'_0$ such that the
Fourier–Deligne transform of [def-fd-transform] of the middle extension
of [def-wf-middle-extension] satisfies

$$
\operatorname{FT}_\psi\bigl((j_*\mathcal M)[1]\bigr)\cong
(j'_*\mathcal M')[1].
$$

proof.text: Put $P=(j_*\mathcal M)[1]$ and $F=\operatorname{FT}_\psi$. By [thm-a1-curve-perverse-heart] the geometric perverse heart and its Weil fixed-pair heart are abelian. By [prop-a1-curve-perverse-simples], $P$ is simple in the Weil heart. The final assertion of [thm-a1-fourier-t-exact] supplies mutually quasi-inverse exact equivalences $F$ and $G=\operatorname{FT}_{\psi^{-1}}(-)(1)$ between the two Weil hearts; it includes the inversion and twist compatibility needed here. Thus $F(P)$ is nonzero: otherwise $P\cong GF(P)=0$. If $0\ne Q\subsetneq F(P)$, exactness gives a subobject $GQ\subset P$ with quotient $G(F(P)/Q)$. Both are nonzero, since applying the inverse equivalence $F$ detects zero objects. This contradicts simplicity of $P$. Consequently $F(P)$ is simple. Applying [prop-a1-curve-perverse-simples] on the dual line, it is either punctual in degree zero or a middle extension of a nonzero irreducible lisse Weil sheaf. The hypotheses hold since both affine lines are smooth separated curves over the perfect finite field; the character is nontrivial.

Suppose the punctual alternative holds, and write $T=\operatorname{For}(F(P))$ for the underlying geometric sheaf. By [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex], forgetting a Weil structure keeps the actual object and arrows on the geometric fiber; no extension-of-base comparison is involved. Let $Z\subset A'$ be its finite reduced support and $i:Z\hookrightarrow A'$. The closed-support essential-image assertion of [lem-a1-qbar-open-closed-cohomology] gives $T\cong i_*i^*T$. Each closed point of $A'=\operatorname{Spec}k[t]$ is $\xi\in k$, since an irreducible polynomial over the algebraically closed field $k$ has degree one. The scheme $Z$ is the finite disjoint union of these points. Clause (3) of [lem-sf-point] identifies a constructible coefficient sheaf at each point with a finite-dimensional $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$-vector space. Choosing bases and using the component inclusions/projections gives
$$T\cong\bigoplus_{\xi\in Z}\delta_\xi^{\oplus n_\xi},\qquad \delta_\xi=i_{\xi*}\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell.$$
Here $n_\xi\ge0$, and at least one is positive: $F(P)\ne0$, and a pair with zero underlying object is zero. All these identifications are geometric; no Frobenius-compatible choice of bases is asserted.

Compute the geometric inverse transform of a summand. In $A'\times_k A$ write $p_1,p_2$ for the projections, $e_\xi:A\hookrightarrow A'\times_k A$ for $x\mapsto(\xi,x)$, and $\mathcal K_{\psi^{-1}}$ for [def-fd-kernel]. Proper base change for $i_\xi$ in [prop-functor-package] gives $p_1^*\delta_\xi\cong e_{\xi*}\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. Its projection formula and the equality of proper direct images give
$$p_1^*\delta_\xi\otimes^L\mathcal K_{\psi^{-1}}\cong Re_{\xi!}e_\xi^*\mathcal K_{\psi^{-1}}.$$
Compact-support composition and its identity equation in that same node, together with $p_2e_\xi=\mathrm{id}_A$, therefore give directly from [def-fd-transform]
$$\operatorname{FT}_{\psi^{-1}}(\delta_\xi)\cong e_\xi^*\mathcal K_{\psi^{-1}}[1]\cong\mathcal L_{\psi^{-1},\xi x}[1]\cong\mathcal L_{\psi,-\xi x}[1].$$
The middle identification is the pullback formula in [def-fd-kernel]; the last is the inverse-character formula of [lem-fd-as-characters]. This is a direct three-formula specialization of the cited six-functor identities, rather than a new lemma. Every scheme is separated and finite type over $k$, $i_\xi,e_\xi$ are proper closed immersions, and the kernel is rank-one lisse. Thus the projection factor is site-perfect and all operations lie in the cited bounded coefficient domains. The argument includes $\xi=0$.

source.place: Step 2, explicitly including the base-change, projection and composition maps

proof.text:
The inverse equivalence in [thm-a1-fourier-t-exact] now gives $P\cong G(F(P))$. By the formula of [def-fd-transform] and the underlying-object convention [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex], forgetting this isomorphism yields the inverse integral transform of the geometric object $T$, followed by $(1)$. The transform is additive (its underlying functor is exact triangulated as stated in [def-fd-transform]), so the preceding two steps give
$$\operatorname{For}(P)\cong\bigoplus_{\xi\in Z}\mathcal L_{\psi,-\xi x}^{\oplus n_\xi}[1](1).$$
The geometric Tate object is isomorphic to the unit: in [def-wf-tate-twist], choose compatible primitive $\ell^r$th roots in the algebraically closed $k$. They identify the inverse system $\mu_{\ell^r}$ with $\mathbf Z/\ell^r$ and its limit with $\mathbf Z_\ell$, hence trivialize $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell(1)$. This choice need not respect Frobenius, which has already been forgotten. Apply $j^*$ and ordinary cohomology in degree $-1$. The exact pullback and $j^*j_*\cong\mathrm{id}$ in [lem-a1-qbar-open-closed-cohomology] give
$$\mathcal M_k\cong\bigoplus_{\xi\in Z}(\mathcal L_{\psi,-\xi x}|_U)^{\oplus n_\xi}.$$
Here $j_*$ is the ordinary sheaf direct image, as specified in [def-wf-middle-extension], not the full derived direct image.

source.place: Step 3, inverse transform, geometric twist and restriction

proof.text: Choose $\xi$ with $n_\xi>0$. By [lem-fd-as-characters] the sheaf $\mathcal L_{\psi,-\xi x}$ is lisse of rank one; its restriction to the nonempty connected open $U$ is still rank one and irreducible. Inclusion and projection of one summand in the displayed decomposition exhibit $\mathcal L_{\psi,-\xi x}|_U$ as a geometric irreducible constituent of $\mathcal M$. This is excluded by [def-a1-constituent-nonexceptional] with $a=-\xi\in k$, including $a=0$ when $\xi=0$. Thus the punctual alternative is impossible. The remaining alternative of [prop-a1-curve-perverse-simples] supplies a dense open $j':U'_0\hookrightarrow A'_0$ and a nonzero irreducible lisse Weil sheaf $\mathcal M'$ with $F(P)\cong(j'_*\mathcal M')[1]$, as required. No geometric irreducibility or semisimplicity of the input has been assumed.

blueprint_update.statement:
In the conventions of [rem-dl-a1-conventions], let $\psi$ be a
nontrivial additive character of $k_0$, let
$j:U_0\hookrightarrow A_0$ be a dense open immersion and let
$\mathcal M$ be a nonzero irreducible lisse Weil sheaf on $U_0$ which is
constituent-nonexceptional in the sense of
[def-a1-constituent-nonexceptional]. Then there are a dense open
immersion $j':U'_0\hookrightarrow A'_0$ into the dual line and a nonzero
irreducible lisse Weil sheaf $\mathcal M'$ on $U'_0$ such that the
Fourier–Deligne transform of [def-fd-transform] of the middle extension
of [def-wf-middle-extension] satisfies

$$
\operatorname{FT}_\psi\bigl((j_*\mathcal M)[1]\bigr)\cong
(j'_*\mathcal M')[1].
$$

proof.text:
Write $\mathrm{Perv}(A_0)$ and $\mathrm{Perv}(A'_0)$ for the perverse
hearts of [def-per-perverse-subcategories] on the two lines. We use three
facts about these hearts.

- **(H1)** The two perverse classes form a t-structure whose heart is
  abelian, with the sheaf-level description on a curve
  ([thm-a1-curve-perverse-heart]).
- **(H2)** $\operatorname{FT}_\psi$ is t-exact: it sends
  $\mathrm{Perv}(A_0)$ into $\mathrm{Perv}(A'_0)$, and
  $\operatorname{FT}_{\psi^{-1}}$ sends $\mathrm{Perv}(A'_0)$ into
  $\mathrm{Perv}(A_0)$ ([thm-a1-fourier-t-exact]).
- **(H3)** The simple objects of the curve heart are the punctual
  $i_{x*}E$, with $x$ a closed point and $E$ an irreducible Weil module
  at $x$ placed in degree $0$, and the $(j_*\mathcal N)[1]$, with
  $\mathcal N$ a nonzero irreducible lisse Weil sheaf on a dense open;
  each of these is simple ([prop-a1-curve-perverse-simples]).

*Step 1: the transform is simple.* By (H3),
$P:=(j_*\mathcal M)[1]$ is a simple object of $\mathrm{Perv}(A_0)$, and
by (H2) $\operatorname{FT}_\psi(P)$ lies in $\mathrm{Perv}(A'_0)$. Put
$G:=\operatorname{FT}_{\psi^{-1}}(-)(1)$, using the Tate twist of
[def-wf-tate-twist]. Fourier inversion [lem-fd-inversion] with $r=1$
gives $\operatorname{FT}_{\psi^{-1}}\operatorname{FT}_\psi(K)\cong K(-1)$,
hence $G\circ\operatorname{FT}_\psi\cong\operatorname{id}$. Applied to the
character $\psi^{-1}$ it gives
$\operatorname{FT}_\psi\operatorname{FT}_{\psi^{-1}}(M)\cong M(-1)$, and
the Tate-twist clause of base linearity [prop-base-linear] (the twist
being the pullback of the twisting object of the base) gives
$\operatorname{FT}_\psi\bigl(\operatorname{FT}_{\psi^{-1}}(M)(1)\bigr)\cong
\operatorname{FT}_\psi\operatorname{FT}_{\psi^{-1}}(M)(1)\cong M$, i.e.
$\operatorname{FT}_\psi\circ G\cong\operatorname{id}$. Hence
$\operatorname{FT}_\psi(P)\neq0$.

By (H2) both functors are exact functors between the abelian hearts of
(H1). Let $0\neq Q\subsetneq\operatorname{FT}_\psi(P)$ be a proper
nonzero subobject. Then $G(Q)\to G\operatorname{FT}_\psi(P)\cong P$ is a
monomorphism. Its source $G(Q)$ is nonzero, and its cokernel
$G\bigl(\operatorname{FT}_\psi(P)/Q\bigr)$ is nonzero, because
$\operatorname{FT}_\psi\circ G\cong\operatorname{id}$ detects zero
objects. This contradicts the simplicity of $P$. So
$\operatorname{FT}_\psi(P)$ is simple, and by (H3) it is either
punctual or of the form $(j'_*\mathcal M')[1]$, with $\mathcal M'$
nonzero, irreducible and lisse on a dense open $U'_0$.

*Step 2: transforms of punctual objects.* Let $\xi\in k$ and let
$\delta_\xi$ be the skyscraper sheaf $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ at
$\xi$ on the geometric dual line $A'$, in degree $0$. We claim

$$
\operatorname{FT}_{\psi^{-1}}(\delta_\xi)\cong\mathcal L_{\psi(-\xi x)}[1]
\quad\text{on }A.
$$

The case $\xi=0$ is the second formula of [lem-fd-first-formula], and
the general case uses the same computation. In the transform from $A'$
to $A$, the pullback of $\delta_\xi$ along the first projection is
supported on $\{\xi\}\times A$. The second projection restricts to an
isomorphism from this line onto $A$. On the line, the kernel of
[def-fd-kernel] for the character $\psi^{-1}$ restricts to
$\mathcal L_{\psi^{-1}(\xi x)}$. By [lem-fd-as-characters] this is
$\mathcal L_{\psi^{-1},\xi x}\cong\mathcal L_{\psi,-\xi x}
=\mathcal L_{\psi(-\xi x)}$. The compactly supported direct image
along an isomorphism is the sheaf itself, and the shift $[1]$ of
[def-fd-transform] gives the claim.

*Step 3: the punctual case is excluded.* Suppose
$\operatorname{FT}_\psi(P)\cong i_{x*}E$ is punctual. Apply $G$ and use
Step 1:

$$
(j_*\mathcal M)[1]\cong\operatorname{FT}_{\psi^{-1}}(i_{x*}E)(1).
$$

Pass to the geometric base change, which commutes with the transform by
[lem-fd-base-change]. After this base change, $i_{x*}E$ becomes a
finite direct sum of copies of skyscrapers $\delta_\xi$ at the geometric
points $\xi$ over $x$. The Tate twist becomes trivial. So Step 2 gives

$$
(j_*\mathcal M)_{\bar k}[1]\cong
\bigoplus_{\xi}\mathcal L_{\psi(-\xi x)}^{\oplus n_\xi}[1],
\qquad\text{hence}\qquad
\mathcal M_{\bar k}\cong\bigoplus_\xi
\bigl(\mathcal L_{\psi(-\xi x)}|_U\bigr)^{\oplus n_\xi}
$$

after restriction to $U$, using $j^*j_*\mathcal M=\mathcal M$. Since
$\mathcal M\neq0$, some $n_\xi>0$. Every geometric irreducible
constituent of $\mathcal M$ is then some $\mathcal L_{\psi(ax)}|_U$
with $a=-\xi\in k$, where $a=0$ is allowed. This contradicts
constituent-nonexceptionality in [def-a1-constituent-nonexceptional].

Therefore $\operatorname{FT}_\psi\bigl((j_*\mathcal M)[1]\bigr)$ is a
simple object of the second kind in (H3), which is the assertion.

The hypothesis is needed. Conversely, the transform of a linear
character is punctual: for $a=0$, $\operatorname{FT}_\psi$ of the
constant sheaf is $\delta_0(-1)[-1]$ by [lem-fd-first-formula]. Hence
an input with an exceptional geometric constituent can have a punctual
simple constituent in its transform.
